lines.title: Evans Gambit: 4.b4
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Ba5 6. d4 exd4 7. O-O d6 8. cxd4 Bb6 9. Nc3
lines.lineSummary: The Evans Gambit sacrifices a pawn for rapid development and a powerful center. A favorite of Kasparov.
lines.strategicGoal: Sacrifice b4 to gain time and build a strong d4+e4 center. Develop rapidly and attack the king.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black tries to hold the pawn with ...Ba5 and ...b5, falling behind in development.
lines.punishmentIdea: After c3-d4, White has a massive center and lead in development. Nc3 and Ba3 create threats.
lines.hintText: After 4.b4 Bxb4 5.c3, the bishop must move again. You gain 2 tempi and a strong center.

lines.title: Two Knights: 4.Ng5 Attack
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Na5 6. Bb5+ c6 7. dxc6 bxc6 8. Be2 h6 9. Nf3 e4 10. Ne5
lines.lineSummary: The Fried Liver/Two Knights Attack where White plays Ng5 targeting f7. Extremely sharp play.
lines.strategicGoal: Attack f7 with Ng5. After ...d5 exd5 Na5, play Bb5+ to disrupt Black's coordination.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...Nxd5 instead of ...Na5, allowing the Fried Liver Nxf7 sacrifice.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Nxd5, Nxf7! Kxf7 Qf3+ leads to a devastating attack on the exposed king.
lines.hintText: 4.Ng5 is the sharpest try. If Black plays ...Nxd5, you get the Fried Liver with Nxf7!

lines.title: Giuoco Pianissimo: Quiet Italian
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. d3 Nf6 5. O-O d6 6. c3 a6 7. a4 Ba7 8. Nbd2 O-O 9. Re1
lines.lineSummary: The Giuoco Pianissimo (very quiet game) — White develops slowly but solidly, preparing d4 break.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop with d3, O-O, c3, then prepare the d4 central break. Nbd2-f1-g3 is the maneuver.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays passively without ...a6 and ...Ba7, allowing a4-a5 to trap the bishop.
lines.punishmentIdea: If Black's bishop stays on c5, a4-a5 can trap it. White's slow buildup leads to a strong d4 break.
lines.hintText: The Pianissimo is about patience. Develop everything, then break with d4 when fully prepared.

lines.title: Fried Liver Attack: Nxf7
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Nxd5 6. Nxf7 Kxf7 7. Qf3+ Ke6 8. Nc3
lines.lineSummary: The famous Fried Liver Attack — White sacrifices a knight on f7 to expose Black's king in the center.
lines.strategicGoal: After Nxf7 Kxf7 Qf3+, Black's king is dragged to e6 where it faces a massive attack.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black recaptures ...Nxd5 instead of the safer ...Na5, walking into the Fried Liver.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Ke6, Nc3 attacks d5 and the king is stuck in the center. White develops with tempo.
lines.hintText: The Fried Liver works when Black plays ...Nxd5. After Nxf7! Kxf7 Qf3+, the king is exposed.

lines.title: vs Hungarian Defense: 3...Be7
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Be7 4. d4 d6 5. dxe5 dxe5 6. Qxd8+ Bxd8 7. Nc3 Nf6 8. Bg5
lines.lineSummary: Against the passive Hungarian Defense (3...Be7), White gets a comfortable advantage with d4.
lines.strategicGoal: Push d4 immediately to open the center. After queens trade, White has better development.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...Be7 passively, giving White a free hand in the center with d4.
lines.punishmentIdea: After d4 dxe5 dxe5 Qxd8+, the endgame favors White with better piece activity and Bg5 pin.
lines.hintText: Against 3...Be7, play d4 immediately. Black's passive setup gives you a free center.

lines.title: Traxler Counterattack: 4...Bc5
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Ng5 Bc5 5. Nxf7 Bxf2+ 6. Kf1 Qe7 7. Nxh8 d5 8. exd5 Nd4
lines.lineSummary: The Traxler Counterattack — Black sacrifices the rook for a ferocious attack against White's king.
lines.strategicGoal: Accept the rook with Nxf7-h8, but be prepared for Black's fierce counterattack with ...d5 and ...Nd4.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays Kxf2 instead of Kf1, walking into a stronger attack.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Kf1 (not Kxf2!), White keeps the extra material. Careful defense leads to a winning endgame.
lines.hintText: Against the Traxler, take on f7 but go Kf1 (not Kxf2). You're up material if you survive.

lines.title: Deutz Gambit: 4.O-O Nxe4 5.d4
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. O-O Nf6 5. d4 Bxd4 6. Nxd4 Nxd4 7. f4 d6 8. fxe5 dxe5 9. Bg5
lines.lineSummary: White sacrifices the d-pawn to open lines and develop rapidly. The f4 push adds to the attack.
lines.strategicGoal: Sacrifice d4 to open the center, then f4 to open the f-file. Bg5 pins and creates threats.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black captures on d4 with both pieces, falling behind in development.
lines.punishmentIdea: After f4 and Bg5, White has open lines and active pieces against Black's undeveloped position.
lines.hintText: After d4 Bxd4 Nxd4 Nxd4, play f4! Opening the f-file with Bg5 gives tremendous compensation.

lines.title: Anti-Berlin: 3.Bc4 vs ...Nf6
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d3 Be7 5. O-O O-O 6. Re1 d6 7. a4 Na5 8. Ba2 c5 9. c3
lines.lineSummary: A quiet approach against ...Nf6, avoiding the Berlin endgame while keeping Italian-style play.
lines.strategicGoal: Develop solidly with d3, O-O, Re1, then prepare the d4 break with c3 and Nbd2.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...Na5 too early, misplacing the knight on the rim.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Na5, Ba2 keeps the bishop safe and the knight on a5 is out of play. c3-d4 follows.
lines.hintText: This is the modern Italian approach — slow but deadly. Prepare d4 with c3, Nbd2, and Re1.

lines.title: Legal's Mate Trap
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 d6 4. Nc3 Bg4 5. h3 Bh5 6. Nxe5 Bxd1 7. Bxf7+ Ke7 8. Nd5
lines.lineSummary: Legal's famous mate trap — White sacrifices the queen to deliver checkmate with minor pieces.
lines.strategicGoal: Sacrifice the queen with Nxe5, allowing ...Bxd1. Then Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5# is checkmate!
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black grabs the queen with ...Bxd1, not seeing the mating pattern.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bxd1, Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5# is checkmate. Even if Black doesn't take, Nxe5 wins a pawn.
lines.hintText: Legal's Mate: after ...Bg4, play Nxe5! If they take the queen, Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5# is mate.

lines.title: Modern Italian: d3 + Nbd2-f1-g3
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. c3 Nf6 5. d3 d6 6. O-O a6 7. Nbd2 Ba7 8. Re1 O-O 9. Nf1 Be6 10. Ng3
lines.lineSummary: The modern Italian with the Nbd2-f1-g3 maneuver — currently the most popular approach at top level.
lines.strategicGoal: Reroute the knight via Nbd2-f1-g3 to control f5 and support the d4 break.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black doesn't play ...a6 and ...Ba7, allowing a4-a5 to cramp the queenside.
lines.punishmentIdea: Without ...a6, White plays a4-a5 fixing the bishop. Ng3-f5 creates kingside pressure.
lines.hintText: The Nf1-g3 maneuver is key. From g3, the knight eyes f5 and h5, supporting the kingside attack.

lines.title: QGA: 2...dxc4 Main Line
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4 c5 6. O-O a6 7. Qe2 b5 8. Bb3 Bb7 9. Rd1
lines.lineSummary: The Queen's Gambit Accepted — Black takes c4 but White recovers the pawn with superior development.
lines.strategicGoal: Recover the c4 pawn naturally with Bxc4. Develop rapidly and use the open c-file and center.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black tries to hold the c4 pawn with ...b5, weakening the queenside.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...b5, a4 undermines the pawn chain. White gets open lines and targets the weak c6/a6 pawns.
lines.hintText: Don't rush to recapture on c4. Develop with Nf3, e3, then Bxc4 — you'll get it back with interest.

lines.title: Exchange Variation: cxd5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bg5 Be7 6. e3 O-O 7. Bd3 Nbd7 8. Qc2 Re8 9. Nf3 c6 10. O-O
lines.lineSummary: The Exchange QG — White trades on d5 creating a symmetrical pawn structure but with a minority attack plan.
lines.strategicGoal: After cxd5 exd5, launch a minority attack with b4-b5 to create weaknesses on Black's queenside.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays passively without ...c5 break, allowing White's minority attack to succeed.
lines.punishmentIdea: b4-b5 cxb5 axb5 creates an isolated c-pawn or backward pawn on c6 for White to target.
lines.hintText: The Exchange QG is all about the minority attack: Rb1, b4, b5 — target Black's queenside pawns.

lines.title: Catalan Setup: g3 System
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. g3 Be7 5. Bg2 O-O 6. O-O dxc4 7. Qc2 a6 8. a4 Bd7 9. Qxc4
lines.lineSummary: The Catalan — White fianchettoes and uses the long diagonal for lasting pressure. A top-level favorite.
lines.strategicGoal: Fianchetto Bg2 to pressure the long diagonal. Recover c4 pawn and maintain positional pressure.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black holds the c4 pawn too long, falling behind in development.
lines.punishmentIdea: If Black holds c4 with ...b5, a4 undermines it. The Bg2 dominates the long diagonal.
lines.hintText: The Catalan bishop on g2 is a monster. Don't rush — let it work on the long diagonal naturally.

lines.title: vs Slav Setup: 2...c6
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 dxc4 5. a4 Bf5 6. e3 e6 7. Bxc4 Bb4 8. O-O O-O 9. Qe2
lines.lineSummary: Against the Slav (2...c6), White plays a4 to prevent ...b5 and recovers the pawn smoothly.
lines.strategicGoal: Play a4 to stop ...b5, then recover c4 with Bxc4. Develop naturally and press in the center.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...dxc4 without ...Bf5 first, allowing e4 with a strong center.
lines.punishmentIdea: Without ...Bf5, White plays e4 immediately after recapturing on c4, dominating the center.
lines.hintText: Against the Slav, a4 is key — it stops ...b5 and keeps Black's queenside under control.

lines.title: London Move Order: 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.c4
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. Nc3 Be7 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bh4 O-O 7. e3 b6 8. Bd3 Bb7 9. O-O
lines.lineSummary: A flexible move order starting with Nf3 before c4, avoiding some of Black's sharpest responses.
lines.strategicGoal: Nf3 first avoids the Albin Counter-Gambit and Budapest. Then transpose to mainline QG positions.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...b6 too early without ...c5, allowing White to build a dominant center.
lines.punishmentIdea: After premature ...b6, White plays e4 with a massive center. The Bb7 bites on granite.
lines.hintText: 2.Nf3 before c4 is a safe move order — it avoids the Albin and Budapest while keeping QG options.

lines.title: vs Chigorin: 2...Nc6
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 Nc6 3. Nf3 Bg4 4. cxd5 Qxd5 5. Nc3 Qa5 6. d5 Ne5 7. Nxe5 Bxd1 8. Bb5+ c6 9. dxc6
lines.lineSummary: Against the Chigorin (2...Nc6), White can enter sharp tactical lines with cxd5 and d5.
lines.strategicGoal: After cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3, the queen is harassed. d5 pushes the knight and opens tactical possibilities.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...Bg4 and ...Bxd1 thinking they win the queen, but Bb5+ is devastating.
lines.punishmentIdea: After ...Bxd1, Bb5+ c6 dxc6 creates multiple threats. White gets massive compensation.
lines.hintText: Against the Chigorin, cxd5 followed by d5 is the sharpest approach. Tactical fireworks follow.

lines.title: vs Tarrasch: 2...e6 3...c5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c5 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. g3 Nf6 7. Bg2 Be7 8. O-O O-O 9. Bg5
lines.lineSummary: Against the Tarrasch Defense, White gets to target Black's isolated d5 pawn.
lines.strategicGoal: After cxd5 exd5, Black has an IQP. Pressure it with Bg2, Bg5, and piece play against d5.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black doesn't use the IQP dynamically (no ...d4 break), allowing White to blockade and pressure.
lines.punishmentIdea: Blockade d5 with Nc3-d4 or Nf3-d4. In the endgame, the isolated pawn becomes a fatal weakness.
lines.hintText: Against the Tarrasch, you get to play against an IQP. Pressure d5 and aim for a favorable endgame.

lines.title: vs Albin Counter-Gambit: 2...e5
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d4 4. Nf3 Nc6 5. Nbd2 Nge7 6. g3 Ng6 7. Bg2 Bg4 8. O-O
lines.lineSummary: The Albin Counter-Gambit where Black sacrifices a pawn for central initiative. White must play carefully.
lines.strategicGoal: Accept the pawn with dxe5, then develop solidly. The extra pawn and Bg2 give White an edge.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White plays e3 too early, blocking the dark-squared bishop and allowing ...d3 tricks.
lines.punishmentIdea: Develop with Nf3, g3, Bg2 — avoid e3! The fianchetto controls the long diagonal and supports the extra pawn.
lines.hintText: Against the Albin, DON'T play e3 (allows ...d3 tricks). Play Nf3, g3, Bg2 instead.

lines.title: Elephant Trap
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 Nbd7 5. cxd5 exd5 6. Nxd5 Nxd5 7. Bxd8 Bb4+ 8. Qd2 Bxd2+ 9. Kxd2 Kxd8
lines.lineSummary: The Elephant Trap — a famous QGD trap where Black wins White's queen with a discovered check.
lines.strategicGoal: AVOID this trap! After Nxd5, Black has ...Bb4+ winning the queen. White must play 6.e3 instead.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: White greedily captures Nxd5 thinking they win a pawn, missing ...Bb4+ discovered attack.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Nxd5?? Bb4+! White must interpose the queen, and after Bxd2+ Kxd2, Black has won the queen for a bishop.
lines.hintText: BEWARE the Elephant Trap! After ...Nbd7 and cxd5 exd5, do NOT play Nxd5 — play e3 instead.

lines.title: Bf4 System (Anti-QGD)
lines.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Bf4 Bd6 5. Bxd6 Qxd6 6. Nc3 O-O 7. e3 c6 8. Bd3 Nbd7 9. O-O
lines.lineSummary: The Bf4 system avoids the mainline QGD theory. White exchanges dark-squared bishops for a simple edge.
lines.strategicGoal: Exchange on d6 to eliminate Black's good bishop, then build up with e3, Bd3, O-O and press.
lines.commonOpponentMistake: Black plays ...Bd6 allowing the exchange, giving White the easier game.
lines.punishmentIdea: After Bxd6 Qxd6, White has eliminated Black's best minor piece. The position is slightly better for White.
lines.hintText: Bf4 is a low-theory way to play the QG. Exchange on d6 and enjoy a risk-free slight edge.
